correctness.rationale: For every dimension \(n\ge2\), averaging positive-definite quadratic pullbacks over the permutation group preserves both bounds in a quadratic sandwich, yielding a symmetric candidate \(Q_t\). A two-vector obstruction rules out \(t<0\). For every \(t\ge0\), the proof establishes the globally sharp Rayleigh extrema \(L=(1+nt)/(1+(n-1)t)\) and \(U=\max\{1+nt,2+c_nt\}\), with explicit achieving vectors and all sign/boundary cases. The derivative sign of their quotient is resolved for every dimension, including the interior minima at \(n=5,6\) and the threshold \(n=7\). Finite pseudorandom checks and witness replay corroborate but do not replace the proof; there is no unproved intermediate lemma.

value.rationale: This is a natural all-dimensional exact classification of the Hilbert distance of finite sections of a named classical Bynum norm, motivated by the 1972 and 2001 studies of geometric renormings and their Banach–Mazur distances. It establishes a sharp dimension-seven phase transition in optimal ellipsoid shape, and strict finite-dimensional improvements including \(d_5=7/5\). The explicit equality vectors and scalar formula support future quantitative comparisons of renormed geometric invariants; it is not an arbitrary finite computation or a routine change of notation.
